item.title: Former Trump aide claims Obama's Cheesecake Factory quip triggered Trump's self-sabotage ahead of midterms
item.description: Miles Taylor, former chief of staff at the Department of Homeland Security under President Trump, has written in his DEFIANCE.org newsletter that former President Barack Obama's joke about Cheesecake Factory 'baited' Trump into making a self-defeating political move days before the midterms. Taylor, who anonymously authored a 2018 New York Times op-ed criticizing Trump, argues that Obama's quip at a Cleveland rally—where he compared Trump's White House to 'Saddam Hussein opening a Cheesecake Factory'—prompted Trump to spend days defending his lavish White House renovations, including gold trim, marble, and a ballroom. Taylor writes that Trump's response, including calling Obama a 'lousy president' on Truth Social and at a Mississippi rally, was 'the worst, most self-defeating closing argument in American election history.' item.title: Ohio restaurant owner and Trump supporter Adam Radogna charged with possessing child sexual abuse material
item.description: Adam Radogna, a 37-year-old restaurant owner from Brook Park, Ohio, and a prominent supporter of former President Donald Trump, has been indicted on 10 felony charges related to the alleged possession of child sexual abuse material. According to reports from WEWS-TV, a Cuyahoga County grand jury issued the indictment on Wednesday. Radogna faces two counts of illegal use of a minor or impaired person in nudity-oriented material or performance, seven counts of pandering sexually oriented matter involving a minor or impaired person, and one count of possessing criminal tools. The charges stem from a search conducted by the Ohio Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force at Radogna's residence on October 22, during which authorities discovered multiple files containing child sexual abuse material on his devices. Radogna was released on a $75,000 bond with conditions including home detention and surrendering his passports. He is scheduled for arraignment at a later date. Radogna, known as

item.title: Iranian Diplomat Challenges US Ambassador at UN Over School Attack in Minab
item.description: Iranian envoy Gholamhossein Darzi confronted US Ambassador Mike Waltz at a United Nations Security Council meeting on Wednesday, displaying photographs of children and other victims of the Minab school attack. Darzi accused the United States of targeting Iran's civilian infrastructure and challenged Waltz to explain the deaths of children in a school strike in Minab. The school, Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School for Girls, was reportedly struck on the first day of the war involving the US, Israel, and Iran. Iranian officials stated that at least 160 schoolchildren and teachers were killed, with more than 95 others injured. Iranian authorities have cited higher death tolls, ranging from 168 to around 170 children. Darzi also rejected US allegations against Iran, stating that Washington had failed to provide a convincing justification for military action against Tehran. He accused the US of making unsubstantiated claims about Iran's nuclear program to divert attention from its own actions

item.title: Fox News shifts Senate race forecasts, signaling potential GOP losses in key states
item.description: Fox News has updated its Power Rankings to reflect a shift in the political landscape ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. The network moved South Carolina's Senate race from a leaning Republican to a toss-up, despite President Donald Trump winning the state by 18 points in 2024. The forecast also adjusted Ohio's Senate race from a toss-up to leaning Democratic, with former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown leading Republican Senator Jon Husted 52% to 47% in a recent Fox News poll. Fox News anchor Ryan Schmelz noted that South Carolina has traditionally been a GOP stronghold, making the shift concerning for Republicans. The forecast projects Democrats will secure 48 Senate seats, Republicans 46, with six races remaining toss-ups. Republicans would retain control with 50 seats due to Vice President JD Vance's tie-breaking vote. item.title: Trump's Defense of Senator Marshall Deepens Controversy Amid Election Challenges
item.description: President Donald Trump's recent efforts to defend Senator Roger Marshall (R-KS) against a medical-debt scandal have backfired, according to a report from Zeteo's 'First Draft' newsletter. Trump's remarks at a rally, where he compared Marshall to 'Shylock' from Shakespeare's 'The Merchant of Venice,' a reference long considered antisemitic, have drawn criticism from his own advisers. The president falsely claimed that Marshall was 'required by law' to pursue debt collection, despite a New York Times investigation revealing that Marshall, an OB-GYN, had sued 700 patients with 18% interest charges and some facing bank account garnishment. The controversy has intensified Marshall's already tight race against Democrat Adam Hamilton, a pastor, with protesters interrupting a campaign event by shouting 'He sued his patients!' item.title: Trump's rally claims face criticism as empty seats and polling data contradict his statements
item.description: President Donald Trump began his Thursday by claiming his rally crowds were the largest in midterm election history and that his approval rating among Republicans had reached 99%. However, critics and fact-checkers quickly refuted these claims. Trump posted on Truth Social that he was drawing 'the BIGGEST CROWDS at Trump Rallies in the history of Midterm Elections, by a factor of five times,' and that his Republican approval rating was at 99%. The anti-Trump group Republicans Against Trump pointed out that Trump's rallies often take place in small arenas with many empty seats, citing a Fox News poll showing his approval rating among Republicans at 76%. Sarah Longwell, publisher of The Bulwark and a former anti-Trump Republican strategist, responded with a sarcastic call to 'SOMEONE PUT HIM IN A HOME AND FEED HIM PUDDING.' item.title: Democrats Gain Ground in Key Senate Races as Midterms Approach
item.description: CNN's latest surveys across four pivotal Senate battlegrounds reveal a shifting political landscape, with Democrats holding leads in Michigan and Texas while races in Kansas and Maine remain tightly contested. In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed holds a 49% to 42% lead over Republican Mike Rogers, with 95% of Democratic likely voters supporting him following the August primary. Rogers' unfavorable rating has risen to 50%, up from 42% in early September. In Texas, Democrat James Talarico leads Republican Ken Paxton 49% to 43%, securing 63% of Latino likely voters and 22% of likely voters of color who supported Trump in 2024. Paxton faces unfavorable views even among some Republicans. Kansas sees a close contest between Democrat Adam Hamilton (49%) and Senator Roger Marshall (45%), with 59% of Hamilton's supporters citing opposition to Marshall as their primary motivation. item.title: Trian-led group proposes $1.4 billion acquisition of Wendy's to enable long-term turnaround
item.description: The Trian Fund Management, led by Nelson Peltz, has made a $1.4 billion cash offer to purchase Wendy's, a struggling fast-food chain, at $7.35 per share. This represents a 20% premium over Wendy's market valuation of $1.2 billion as of Tuesday's close. The offer, confirmed by FOX Business and disclosed in a regulatory filing, was first reported by The Wall Street Journal. The Trian-led group, which includes restaurant operator Flynn Group and investment firms BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street Partners, argues that taking Wendy's private would allow for a more effective long-term turnaround strategy requiring significant capital investment over multiple years. Wendy's shares have declined approximately 68% over the past five years, though they surged nearly 17% on Wednesday following the announcement. item.title: Defense Secretary Hegseth faces growing congressional opposition amid budget disputes and Iran war concerns
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is encountering increasing resistance from both Democratic and Republican lawmakers on Capitol Hill, according to a recent Washington Post report. The report, based on interviews with 30 individuals involved in congressional national security matters, indicates that Hegseth's combative communication style has damaged bipartisan cooperation that has historically facilitated the passage of defense bills. During his first private meeting with the Senate Armed Services Committee in June 2025, Hegseth reportedly expressed distrust of committee members, stating he would be cautious about what he said in classified sessions. In April, he criticized congressional Democrats and some Republicans as 'reckless, feckless and defeatist,' a comment that drew strong rebuke from Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), who called it 'shockingly unprofessional.' item.title: Trump's anger over Epstein remarks leads to social media outburst as aides adjust to his insular circle
item.description: A recent report from The New York Times details a significant outburst by President Donald Trump following a segment on Bill Maher's HBO show that referenced his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. Trump, who tuned in expecting a favorable segment about his former press secretary Karoline Leavitt, became enraged when Maher instead made jokes about Epstein and a White House dinner, quipping that he 'could not have been treated better if I was Russian.' In response, Trump dictated a 1,300-word social media post on Truth Social, calling Maher a 'Loser' and vowing never to watch his show again. The incident highlights the increasingly insular nature of Trump's inner circle, with close aide Natalie Harp, 35, now working from the president's private dining room instead of her usual desk outside the Oval Office. item.title: Melania Trump Claims Credit for Ukraine Ceasefire That Was Secured by Pope Leo XI
item.description: The article criticizes Melania Trump for falsely claiming credit for securing a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine, which was actually initiated by Pope Leo XI. The Pope, recovering from lung cancer surgery, contacted Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy to facilitate humanitarian aid delivery. Melania's false assertion at the United Nations, where she positioned herself as the 'exclusive intermediary,' contradicts the facts and undermines the Pope's efforts. The article highlights Melania's pattern of taking credit for others' achievements, including a 2016 speech similar to Michelle Obama's. It also discusses her personal attacks on critics, such as Joanne Carducci, a political influencer who criticized Melania's women's empowerment initiatives. The piece emphasizes Melania's unpopularity as First Lady, her lack of genuine connection to the role, and her husband's influence on her behavior. item.title: ICE Detainee Who Died in Texas Facility Was Lawful Permanent Resident, Family Says
item.description: A 56-year-old lawful permanent resident of the United States, Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias, died in ICE custody at a for-profit detention center in Laredo, Texas. According to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), he was arrested in June at a border crossing after being suspected of obtaining legal status through fraudulent means by not disclosing a 2004 theft arrest. However, his daughter disputes this, stating that immigration authorities were aware of the arrest when they approved his green card application. DHS referred to him as a 'criminal alien' in their statement without providing evidence of a criminal conviction. The Rio Grande Processing Center, operated by the for-profit GEO Group, where Andrade-Covarrubias was held, has faced criticism for not conducting required health assessments for new detainees within two weeks, as noted in a January 2025 ICE inspection report. His family claims he was denied necessary medical care for pre-existing conditions including high blood

item.title: Arizona GOP's transformation under MAGA influence raises concerns over party's future
item.description: A veteran Arizona operative who helped launch John McCain’s Senate career, Chuck Coughlin of HighGround polling firm, has declared that the state’s Republican Party has been hollowed out by MAGA (Make America Great Again) ideology, stating the party 'functionally doesn't even exist anymore.' Coughlin, who runs a polling firm, told MS NOW that moderate Republicans no longer exist in Arizona, with the party now dominated by Turning Point, a conservative group that has poured $18 million into a media blitz to support Rep. Andy Biggs, the Trump-endorsed former House Freedom Caucus chair. Biggs, who backed efforts to overturn the 2020 election results, is currently trailing Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs in polls, with HighGround showing Hobbs leading by nearly 17 points among Republicans and independents. A separate Equis Research survey indicated Hobbs ahead by about 7 points, with roughly 1 in 10 of Trump’s 2024 voters supporting her. The Republican ticket includes election deniers such as

item.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar Rules Update: Major Changes for Khazalite Holds and Sons of Behemat
item.description: The latest rules update for Warhammer Age of Sigmar introduces significant changes to several factions, with major updates affecting Khazalite Holds and Sons of Behemat. The Khazalite Holds faction has undergone a keyword transition, converting older FYRESLAYERS keywords to the new GRIMMDRON, ensuring compatibility with updated rules. This adjustment allows players to continue using established units like the Fyreslayers Scourge of Aqshy without disruption. Additionally, the Lofnir Drothkeepers Army of Renown has been slightly rewritten to better align with new rules, featuring an enhanced method for generating grudge marks when Magmadroths are defeated. For the Sons of Behemat, the update addresses a long-standing issue where players struggled to field legally compliant 2,000-point armies without relying on auxiliary units. item.title: Conservative Radio Host Erick Erickson Refuses to Back Georgia GOP Senate Candidate
item.description: Conservative radio host Erick Erickson has declared he will not vote for Georgia's Republican Senate nominee, Mike Collins, sparking a heated online dispute with Trump campaign aide Tim Murtaugh. Erickson, host of the nationally syndicated 'Erick Erickson Show' and contributor to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, wrote in a recent column that he will leave the Senate ballot line blank rather than support Collins, who is running against Democratic incumbent Jon Ossoff. He criticized the Republican Party for repeatedly pushing 'bad candidates' and argued that America remains intact despite worsening political choices. Former Georgia GOP Chairman David Shafer dismissed Erickson's decision as 'foolish,' stating that candidates are chosen in open primaries, not by the party. Murtaugh, a former Trump campaign communications strategist, accused Erickson of 'torch[ing] his own career' and claimed Erickson's stance would empower left-wing policies. item.title: Short, Frequent Exercise Sessions May Offer Comparable Strength Gains to Traditional Workouts, Study Shows
item.description: A recent study conducted by researchers at Tongji University in China has revealed that breaking resistance training into short, frequent sessions throughout the day can produce strength and endurance gains similar to those achieved through a single, continuous workout. The eight-week experiment involved 45 young male participants aged 18 to 25 who regularly lifted weights. Participants were divided into two groups: one performing three 1-minute sessions of 20 weighted squats each (totaling 60 squats), and the other completing a single 60-squat session. Both groups used a Smith machine under expert supervision, with weights progressively increased over time. At the study's conclusion, researchers found no significant differences in relative muscular endurance or strength between the two training methods. The only notable difference was that participants who engaged in 'exercise snacking' reported greater enjoyment. The study authors suggest that distributing training into multiple shor

item.title: House Republicans' Midterm Prospects Tied to Troubled Incumbents
item.description: The upcoming midterm election has become a critical juncture for House Republicans, who face significant challenges in maintaining their majority amid a series of missteps by key incumbents. According to Cook Political Report, Democrats are poised to win 186 of the 435 House seats, with a clear advantage in 34 others, while Republicans hold firm control in only 168 races and have an advantage in 30. This leaves 17 races in play, with Republicans needing to win all toss-up races and three Democratic-leaning contests to secure a majority. However, several Republican incumbents have made strategic errors that could cost them their seats. Rep. Tom Barrett (R-MI) faces criticism for his unfulfilled promises regarding a veterans' institute, with Harvard University's Election Forecaster giving his opponent a 92% chance of victory. Rep. Rob Bresnahan (R-PA) has been criticized for falsely claiming credit for ending a 'rain tax,' which was actually part of a Trump executive order, and for tradi

item.title: Neural Mechanisms Link Reinforcement Learning to Motor Efficiency in Aplysia Feeding Circuit
item.description: A groundbreaking study published in Communications Biology has uncovered how reinforcement learning shapes both the selection of motor actions and the timing of their execution in the Aplysia feeding circuit. Researchers led by Yuto Momohara, Curtis L. Neveu, and John H. Byrne from the University of Texas Health Science Center conducted experiments using an ex vivo operant conditioning paradigm on the Aplysia feeding circuit. Their findings reveal that reinforcement biases motor program selection toward ingestive behaviors while simultaneously shortening the duration of these actions by advancing the transition from protraction to retraction phases in feeding movements. The study identified specific neural mechanisms underlying this temporal compression, demonstrating that operant conditioning reduces the intrinsic electrical excitability of neuron B52, which weakens B52-mediated inhibition of the retraction-initiating interneuron B64. This adjustment lowers the threshold for triggerin

item.title: Practical Strategies to Manage 'What If' Anxiety Before It Escalates
item.description: The Washington Post article 'How to stop a 'what if' anxiety spiral before it takes over' by Anna Borges discusses the common experience of anxiety spirals that begin with a single worry and escalate into catastrophic thinking. The author explains how a simple concern, such as a date going poorly, a work mistake, or an unusual medical test result, can quickly spiral into overwhelming 'what if' scenarios like 'What if I never find someone?' or 'What if I'm dying?'. The article provides four practical strategies from a psychologist to interrupt this worst-case thinking pattern. These include recognizing the spiral early, challenging the validity of catastrophic thoughts, grounding oneself in the present moment, and developing a structured plan for potential outcomes. The piece emphasizes that while anxiety is a natural response, it becomes problematic when it leads to persistent negative thinking that impacts daily functioning. The article aims to help readers regain control by offering

item.title: Trump criticizes East Potomac Golf Course conditions, threatens legal action against judge
item.description: President Donald Trump took to Truth Social late Wednesday night to criticize the condition of East Potomac Golf Course in Washington, D.C., calling it 'highly dangerous, dilapidated, and absolutely disgusting.' He posted eight photos showing torn netting, broken railings, exposed rafters, and a patchy driving range. Trump claimed that golf balls were flying through gaps in the netting, hitting unsuspecting golfers, including a White House staffer who was struck in the chest. He labeled the course a 'National Disgrace' and a 'barren, debris-ridden wasteland,' promising to transform it into a 'WORLD CLASS PUBLIC Golf Course that is AFFORDABLE for locals.' Trump also threatened to hold federal judge Ana C. Reyes, who blocked the renovation plans, 'fully responsible' for any injuries or deaths resulting from the course's condition. Reyes, a Biden appointee, recently extended a preliminary injunction barring the government from removing or damaging trees and requiring 10 days' notice befor

item.title: South Carolina Republicans Criticize Trump's Intervention in Senate Race
item.description: South Carolina Republicans are expressing frustration over President Donald Trump's active involvement in the state's Senate race, which they believe is jeopardizing a traditionally safe Republican seat. Trump recently visited South Carolina for the third time in three months, rallying for Senator Darline Graham, the sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who died in July. The president urged Governor H.R. McMaster to appoint Graham to complete her brother's term and later endorsed her bid for a full six-year term. However, several Republican lawmakers and officials now argue that Trump's heavy-handed approach is backfiring, with Graham's campaign struggling to gain traction among voters. Representative Nancy Mace (R-SC) described the situation as a 'f---ing train wreck,' stating that voters are resistant to what they perceive as nepotism. A South Carolina GOP official revealed that private polling shows Graham tied with Democratic challenger Annie Andrews at 48 percent, with only

item.title: House Report Alleges Trump and Epstein Argued Over Sexual Abuse of Minor
item.description: A recent report by the House Judiciary Committee has detailed allegations that Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein engaged in a pattern of sexual abuse involving multiple women, including minors, during the 1990s. The report, which includes testimony from 11 women, focuses on a particularly disturbing account from a woman identified as 'Katie Johnson,' who claims she was 13 years old when she was subjected to repeated sexual and physical abuse by both Trump and Epstein at Epstein's New York residence in 1994. According to Johnson's criminal complaint, she was lured to Epstein's home with promises of money and a modeling career, and during a four-month period, she was abused by both men. The report states that Johnson alleged Trump and Epstein argued over who would take her virginity, with Trump reportedly calling Epstein a 'Jew B----rd' and insisting he should be the one to 'pop the cherry.' item.title: Republican Senator's Religious Test for Office Sparks Constitutionality Debate
item.description: Joe Scarborough, host of MS NOW, became visibly agitated during a live broadcast on Thursday after viewing a clip of Republican Senator Bernie Moreno making remarks about Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, a practicing Muslim. Moreno, campaigning in Ohio, stated that El-Sayed is 'unfit to serve because of his religious beliefs,' arguing that El-Sayed does not understand the concept that 'our rights come from God Almighty, that Jesus came here for our salvation.' Scarborough, a former Republican member of Congress and practicing Baptist, expressed shock at Moreno's comments, emphasizing that the First Amendment explicitly prohibits the establishment of a religion and guarantees religious freedom. He pointed out that the Constitution allows for individuals of any faith, including Muslims, to run for office, stating, 'You can be a Christian, a Jew, a Muslim, an agnostic, an atheist, a Hindu. item.description: IGN commerce editor Chris Reed has identified a current deal at Newegg that allows customers to purchase a $100 PlayStation Store digital gift card for $85, saving $15 through the promo code GTWF2793. This offer, available today only, provides the best discount on PlayStation credit ahead of the November 19 launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. The Ultimate Edition of GTA 6, which includes exclusive vehicles, weapons, and apparel, can be purchased with the $100 credit. item.title: Obama addresses Cheesecake Factory controversy at Georgia rally, mocks Trump's White House decor
item.description: Former President Barack Obama recently addressed the Cheesecake Factory controversy at a 'United for Georgia' rally, where he elaborated on his viral comment comparing President Donald Trump's White House to a Cheesecake Factory. Obama clarified that while Trump was not bothered by the Saddam Hussein reference, he was deeply offended by the Cheesecake Factory mention, claiming the administration mobilized a 'whole of government response' to the joke rather than addressing economic issues like inflation. The former president also criticized Trump's White House decorating choices, noting the president was 'super gluing gold medallions to the mantle in the Oval Office' while the country faced significant challenges. Conservative commentators had previously accused Obama of elitism over the Cheesecake Factory line, with some claiming he 'has never been in a Cheesecake Factory.' item.title: Francis Halzen Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for IceCube Neutrino Observatory Contributions
item.description: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced on October 6 that Belgian-American physicist and astrophysicist Francis Halzen has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. This marks the first unshared Physics Nobel since 1992 and the fifth in history related to neutrinos. Halzen's work bridges particle physics and astrophysics, focusing on the detection of neutrinos, often called 'ghost particles' due to their near-invisibility and ability to pass through matter without interaction. The article details the historical context of neutrino research, from Wolfgang Pauli's 1931 theoretical prediction to the 1956 experimental confirmation by Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines. It highlights key milestones, including Raymond Davis Jr.'s 1968 detection of solar neutrinos and the 1987 Kamiokande II detection of neutrinos from supernova SN 1987A. Halzen's pivotal contri

item.title: Toronto Police Seek Elderly Man After Sexual Assault at School Open House
item.description: Toronto police have issued a public appeal for information regarding a sexual assault that occurred during a school open house event in Scarborough on Tuesday. The incident involved an underage victim who was allegedly assaulted on school grounds by a suspect who attended the open house. According to police reports, the victim managed to stop the assault before the suspect fled the scene on foot. The suspect is described as an elderly male with balding gray and white hair, a gray and white beard, and was last seen wearing a beige jacket, a blue and white plaid button-up shirt, black pants, and black shoes. Police have released a photograph of the suspect to aid in the investigation. The assault reportedly took place in the Guildwood Parkway and Livingston Road area. Authorities are urging anyone with information to contact investigators immediately. This incident has raised concerns about safety at community events, particularly those involving minors. item.title: Republicans express concern over Trump's campaign focus amid declining support
item.description: According to The Atlantic's Jonathan Lemire, Republicans are privately expressing concern that President Donald Trump's final campaign message to voters does not address the issues most important to their supporters. Trump's campaign strategy has reportedly centered on dismissing the affordability crisis, attacking comedian Bill Maher, and praising Senator Jon Husted's physical appearance. During a Michigan rally, Trump referred to Democrat Abdul El-Sayed as a jihadist five times and spent approximately three and a half minutes discussing Husted's football career. At a Mississippi rally, he devoted roughly seven minutes to discussing White House redecorating. Many Republicans, including those within Trump's inner circle, have told Lemire that Trump has lost touch with his base, with his approval ratings falling to the low 30s. Candidates in competitive races, such as Susan Collins in Maine and John Sununu in New Hampshire, have reportedly requested that Trump avoid campaigning in their

item.title: Trump's Legacy of Controversy and Legal Troubles Shapes Midterm Election Narrative
item.description: The article, written by Ray Richmond, a journalist and adjunct professor, argues that the upcoming midterm elections will serve as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency and his ongoing legal and political controversies. The author presents a detailed list of Trump's legal issues, including 34 felony convictions, 4 criminal indictments, and 91 felony counts originally charged, alongside his business failures, such as six corporate bankruptcies. The piece also highlights Trump's impact on American institutions, including the erosion of trust in elections, the peaceful transfer of power, and the independence of the Justice Department. Richmond emphasizes that Trump's actions have led to a deterioration in basic civility, making it difficult to disagree with others without resorting to personal attacks. The article criticizes Trump for his role in undermining scientific expertise, public health institutions, and the educational system, as well as for elevating authoritarian figures lik

item.title: Daily Fiber Supplement Shows Promise in Reducing Knee Arthritis Pain and Enhancing Muscle Strength
item.description: A clinical trial led by researchers at the University of Nottingham has revealed that a daily prebiotic fiber supplement, specifically inulin, can significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis (OA) pain while improving muscle strength. The study, published in the journal Nutrients, involved 117 adults with knee OA who were assigned to one of four treatment groups: inulin alone, digital physical therapy exercises (PSE) alone, a combination of inulin and PSE, or a placebo. Participants taking inulin experienced notable pain reduction, improved grip strength, and decreased pain sensitivity compared to those in the physical therapy group. The supplement also demonstrated a much higher adherence rate, with only 3.6% dropout in the inulin group versus 21% in the physical therapy group. Inulin, a naturally occurring fiber found in foods like chicory root and Jerusalem artichokes, is not broken down by digestive enzymes but instead nourishes beneficial gut bacteria in the large intestine. item.title: Critical UEFI Firmware Flaw Affects Most Servers, Allows Pre-Boot Code Execution
item.description: A critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, has been discovered in the TianoCore EDK II open-source codebase used by most server vendors and data centers for UEFI firmware. The flaw, rated 9.5 out of 10 in severity, is a memory-corruption issue in the ICMP component that allows attackers to execute malicious code before the operating system and firmware defenses like Secure Boot activate. The vulnerability affects the PXE-Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe), which handles network boot processes, enabling attackers to send malicious ICMP error messages that overwrite memory buffers. This can lead to code execution in ring 0, the most privileged CPU level, before security mechanisms like TPM and Secure Boot are engaged. The flaw has been present for 16 years and impacts systems that boot from network resources, including servers, storage equipment, and devices relying on EDK2-based firmware. While the vulnerability requires local network access for exploitation, it poses

item.title: Ukrainian Authorities Face Growing Scrutiny Over Forced Mobilization Practices
item.description: In Ukrainian cities, the routine checks of military registration documents and the forcible transfer of men to Territorial Recruitment Centers (TCCs) have become a common feature of wartime life. TCC personnel and police officers conduct vehicle stops, pedestrian inspections, and joint raids, often using physical force. Mobile teams frequently change locations, with residents warning each other through local Telegram groups. Social media and news outlets have documented cases of beatings, unlawful detentions, and denial of access to lawyers. The Ukrainian ombudsman has reported a significant increase in complaints about these practices, with some cases leading to criminal convictions. However, many convictions result in suspended sentences, allowing offenders to continue serving. The Council of Europe and United Nations have also raised concerns about violations of human rights, including excessive restrictions on conscientious objection. item.title: A Doctor's Unusual Examination and the Words That Left a Patient Shocked
item.description: A recent incident involving a medical examination has sparked discussion about patient-doctor communication and the importance of clear, respectful dialogue in healthcare settings. The patient, who wishes to remain anonymous, described an encounter with a physician who, during a routine gynecological exam, made comments that were both unexpected and unsettling. The doctor reportedly looked at the patient's genital area and then stated three words that the patient found shocking. While the exact words were not disclosed, the patient expressed concern about the appropriateness of the remarks and the lack of explanation provided. This incident highlights the need for healthcare providers to maintain professionalism and ensure that patients feel comfortable and informed during examinations. Medical ethics require that doctors communicate clearly with patients, explaining procedures and any observations made during exams. The patient's experience underscores the potential for misunderstandi

item.title: NME releases 2025-2026 coffee table book featuring 50 emerging artists with exclusive content
item.description: NME has launched 'NME The Cover 2025-2026', a 300-page hardcover coffee table book collecting 50 stories from its weekly franchise that champions emerging artists globally. The third edition in the annually released series features artists such as Maruja, Balu Brigada, Die Spitz, Gigi Perez, BOYNEXTDOOR, and many others, with bespoke artwork, interviews, and previously unseen photography. The book is available for purchase with a 20% launch discount, with orders beginning dispatch on November 6. Free UK delivery is offered, and international shipping is free on orders over £200. Karen Gwee, Managing Editor (Music) at NME Networks, emphasized the mission of breaking new and next music through The Cover, calling it a 'true labour of love.' The Cover relaunched in May 2023 with the goal of connecting emerging artists with NME's audience of millions of music fans. The book includes a full list of featured artists, with additional content available on Spotify and Apple Music. Previous editi

item.title: Sauna Bathing Temporarily Boosts Immune Cell Circulation, Study Finds
item.description: A recent study conducted by researchers in Finland has revealed that a single 30-minute sauna session, followed by a brief cold shower, triggers a temporary surge in white blood cells circulating in the bloodstream. The findings, published in the journal Temperature, indicate that sauna bathing mobilizes immune cells that typically reside in tissues, allowing them to move more freely throughout the body. This increased circulation enhances the body's ability to monitor for pathogens such as bacteria and viruses. The study measured various types of white blood cells, including neutrophils and lymphocytes, which are critical for immune responses. Neutrophils act as first responders to infections, while lymphocytes are involved in recognizing specific threats and producing antibodies. The increase in these cells was observed immediately after the sauna session but returned to baseline levels within 30 minutes. item.title: Faith Domergue: A 1950s Horror and Sci-Fi Star Known for Her Dark Beauty
item.description: Faith Domergue (1924 or 1925–1999) was an American actress celebrated for her dark beauty and significant roles in 1950s science fiction and horror films. Discovered as a teenager by Howard Hughes, she was signed to a contract and groomed for stardom, though her early career faced delays and limited opportunities. Domergue gained lasting recognition in the mid-1950s with appearances in cult classics such as This Island Earth (1955), It Came from Beneath the Sea (1955), and Cult of the Cobra (1955), earning her a place among the era’s early 'scream queens.' Her striking features and intense screen presence made her a distinctive figure in mid-century genre cinema. These films, now considered classics, highlight her ability to captivate audiences with her dramatic presence. Domergue's work in these movies cemented her legacy as a memorable face of 1950s science fiction and film noir. Her career, though not as prolific as some contemporaries, remains influential in the history of genre fi

item.title: Samsung TV's Pet Care feature raises privacy concerns over data sharing with advertisers
item.description: In April 2025, Samsung introduced Vision AI sets with features called Pet Care and Family Care, which could detect dog barks or baby cries in an empty room and send alerts to owners' phones. The company stated these features only worked when the TV was turned off. However, on October 23, 2026, a reverse engineer known as log4j shared findings suggesting Samsung TVs send data about barks, cries, sensor readings, and camera streaming duration to Samsung servers. The researcher discovered this through unpatched security flaws that allowed full control of the TV, revealing sound-classification models, screen capture logs, and cross-device advertising IDs. Samsung's automatic content recognition (ACR) system, which samples screen content twice per second, has been documented for years, but the new claims involve potential audio data collection. The researcher alleges that even when ACR is turned off, data might still be transmitted. Samsung has disputed the claims, stating that viewing-reco

item.title: GOP Strategist Criticizes Ex-Trump Aide's Proposal to Cut Ukraine Funding to End War
item.description: On Wednesday's episode of CNN's 'NewsNight,' guest-hosted by Michael Smerconish, Republican strategist Shermichael Singleton engaged in a heated exchange with Caroline Sunshine, a former Trump White House aide, over her proposal to end the Ukraine-Russia conflict by cutting U.S. funding to Ukraine. Sunshine argued that the U.S. should withdraw financial support to force Ukraine to negotiate a peace deal, stating that Ukraine is not a NATO ally and the U.S. has no role in the war except to end it. Singleton strongly opposed the idea, calling it 'the most absurd thing' and accusing Sunshine of being 'incredibly naive.' He emphasized that Russia, not Ukraine, initiated the conflict, noting that 'it wasn't the Ukrainians. It was the Russians.' Singleton further criticized Sunshine for suggesting that Ukraine should be pressured to negotiate, arguing that the U.S. has never taken such a stance before. item.title: Vali Myers: Australian Artist and Spiritual Pioneer of Positano
item.description: Vali Myers, widely known as the 'Witch of Positano,' was an Australian artist, dancer, and mystic whose life spanned the post-war avant-garde scenes of Paris, New York's Chelsea Hotel, and a remote Italian canyon. Born in Sydney in 1930, Myers became a prominent figure in the Beatnik movement in Paris, where she was photographed by Ed van der Elsken for his book 'Love on the Left Bank.' She associated with cultural icons like Jean Cocteau, Allen Ginsberg, and Jean-Paul Sartre. After overcoming an opium addiction, Myers retreated with her partner Rudi Rappold to a cliffside ravine near Positano, Italy, where they lived in an abandoned stone structure without modern amenities. For decades, she immersed herself in nature, creating intricate pen-and-ink and watercolor drawings that depicted mystical themes, animal forms, and powerful representations of femininity. She also established a wildlife sanctuary for rescued animals, contributing to the area's protection as a WWF oasis. Myers main

item.title: Bluesky Blocks Links to DHS Employee Data Leak, Citing Safety Concerns
item.description: Bluesky has blocked links to a newly leaked archive containing records of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employees and contractors, labeling the pages as 'malicious.' The files include personal contact information such as email addresses and phone numbers, shared without authorization, which violates Bluesky's community guidelines. The company chose to block the links rather than remove individual posts to avoid restricting public discussion or broader access to reporting on the leak. The DHS records, published by the transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), detail employee names, contact information, and internal group memberships, including those tied to surveillance and undercover operations. A WIRED investigation revealed the files provide insight into DHS organizational structure, from leadership to individual immigration agents, and who has access to certain technologies. item.title: Snow Peak Campfield: A Japanese-Inspired Retreat on Washington's Long Beach Peninsula
item.description: Snow Peak Campfield, located on Washington's Long Beach Peninsula, offers a unique blend of Japanese design and Pacific Northwest natural beauty. The campfield features Jyubako suites, small cabins made of pale pine and plywood, each approximately 200 square feet with a queen bed, futon, kitchenette, and private bathroom. Priced from $130 per night, these cabins are designed to encourage guests to stay connected with nature, with low furniture that positions the eye at the top edge of the glass door to the porch, gently nudging guests outside. The main attraction is the Ofuro, a Japanese-style bathhouse with a hot pool maintained at 104 degrees, a hinoki cypress sauna, cold plunge, and showers. The bathhouse is thoughtfully designed with angled beams echoing the surrounding trees and an open side facing a grove of alders at the edge of a pond. The Long Beach Peninsula, where the campfield is situated, is known for its wide sandy beaches, razor clamming, kite flying, and storm watching.

item.title: MUHC Researchers Identify New Vesicles Linked to Cancer Cell Migration and Metastasis
item.description: Researchers at McGill University Health Centre (MUHC) have identified a novel mechanism by which migrating cancer cells communicate and spread throughout the body. The study, led by Prof. Julia Burnier and PhD student Thupten Tsering, reveals that cancer cells release specialized structures called motile vesicles (MoVes), which carry genetic material including cancer-associated mutations. These vesicles, previously thought to be cellular waste, are now understood to play a critical role in cell-to-cell communication during cancer progression. The discovery emerged unexpectedly while investigating how cancer cells release DNA, leading to the identification of MoVes as a key component in the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process. EMT is a biological mechanism that allows cells to become more mobile and invasive, contributing to tumor progression and treatment resistance. item.title: Early Voting by Black Voters Rises in Southern States Ahead of 2026 Midterms
item.description:
Early voting among Black Americans has increased significantly ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, particularly in Southern states where Republican redistricting efforts have targeted majority-Black congressional districts. According to The Bulwark, Black voters have cast more than 160,000 additional ballots compared with the same stage of the 2022 midterm elections, raising questions about whether Republican efforts to reshape electoral districts could have unintended political consequences.
The developments follow the Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, a case that originated in Louisiana and weakened the protections provided by Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. Following the decision, Republicans in several states moved to redraw congressional maps and dismantle majority-Black districts. item.title: Trump Administration Challenges Court Order on Park Closure for Golf Course Renovation
item.description: The Trump administration's Justice Department has raised objections to a federal court order requiring detailed notice before closing East Potomac Park in Washington, D.C., for a golf course renovation. In a filing with the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, the department argued that the court's requirements for 'prompt notice' and extensive documentation, including naming every individual involved and assessing the impact on the park, are overly burdensome. The closure, scheduled for November 15, is part of a plan to replace the current public golf course with a 'World Class, championship-level golf course' designed by Tom Fazio, capable of hosting major tournaments like the U.S. Open and the Ryder Cup. The National Park Service has signed a new lease with National Links Trust, the company currently operating the East Potomac Golf Course, which will cease operations by the closure date but will continue managing Rock Creek and Langston golf courses. item.title: Dancing With the Stars Season 35 Features First Perfect Score and Double Elimination During Horror Movie-Themed Episode
item.description: Dancing With the Stars season 35 celebrated Halloween with a horror movie-themed episode, featuring performances inspired by films such as Saw, Black Swan, and Joker. The episode marked the first perfect score of the season when Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson earned a 40/40 for their contemporary dance to 'Toxic' by 2WEI, inspired by the horror film Saw. This performance placed them at the top of the leaderboard with a combined score of 76/80 after combining scores from both Horror Movie Night and Dedication Night. The episode also saw the elimination of two couples: Jackson Olson and Emma Slater, and Tyler Cameron and Sharna Burgess, who had the lowest combined scores. The elimination was determined by a combination of judges' scores and viewer votes from both Dedication and Horror Movie Night. item.title: Europe moves toward direct talks with Russia amid shifting geopolitical dynamics
item.description: After months of hesitation and internal debate, European leaders are signaling a decisive shift toward direct engagement with Russia to address the Ukraine conflict and reshape continental security architecture. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre recently held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, marking a significant step in Europe's diplomatic approach. While lacking formal mandates, their initiative positioned Nordic leaders as key interlocutors, with the Kremlin confirming plans for continued direct communication. item.title: Desarrollador de Tiny11 logra ejecutar Windows 11 26H2 con 128 MB de RAM, demostrando límites técnicos
item.description: El desarrollador NTDEV, creador de Tiny11, ha logrado ejecutar Windows 11 26H2 utilizando únicamente 128 MB de memoria RAM, una cifra 32 veces inferior al requisito mínimo oficial de 4 GB establecido por Microsoft. Esta versión extremadamente optimizada del sistema operativo permite cargar el escritorio, abrir el Explorador de archivos, mostrar el menú Inicio y ejecutar aplicaciones básicas como el Bloc de notas, aunque con rendimiento muy lento y limitaciones en multitarea. El experimento forma parte de una serie de pruebas realizadas por NTDEV para reducir el consumo de recursos de Windows, habiendo previamente logrado ejecutar el sistema con 184 MB de RAM en modo seguro y utilizando 4 GB de VRAM de una tarjeta gráfica NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 en 2023. Además, el desarrollador está trabajando en Pico11, un proyecto que busca reducir Windows 11 a tamaños mínimos, logrando en octubre de 2026 una imagen ISO de 699.811.840 bytes, suficiente para almacenarse en un CD-ROM convencional. item.title: El euskera: lengua preindoeuropea superviviente en Europa occidental, desmontando mitos históricos
item.description: La noticia analiza el origen de los vascos y el euskera, desmontando mitos populares sobre su antigüedad y singularidad. El euskera es la única lengua preindoeuropea que sobrevivió en Europa occidental tras las migraciones indoeuropeas del segundo milenio antes de Cristo. Aunque se ha asociado con una 'Vieja Europa' inalterada, el euskera moderno ha evolucionado significativamente, absorbiendo influencias léxicas de lenguas como el latín, el celta y el árabe. La investigación histórica y genética refuta teorías raciales y mitos como el 'tubalismo', que atribuía a los vascos un origen divino. El término 'Euzkadi', creado por Sabino Arana, es un neologismo político sin base etimológica real. Los estudios genéticos demuestran que los vascos comparten el mismo acervo genético ibérico que sus vecinos, con el 85% de varones portando el haplogrupo R1b, lo que desmiente la idea de una 'raza pura'. item.title: El descubrimiento accidental de un colorante sintético en 1856 que revolucionó la industria textil
item.description: En 1856, el químico británico William Henry Perkin, de apenas 18 años, intentó sintetizar quinina para tratar la malaria, un medicamento esencial en la época. Durante sus experimentos en un laboratorio casero en Londres, utilizó compuestos derivados del alquitrán de hulla y, en lugar de obtener el medicamento deseado, descubrió accidentalmente un color violeta intenso que teñía la seda con gran intensidad. Este descubrimiento, inicialmente considerado un fracaso, dio lugar a la primera industria de colorantes orgánicos sintéticos. Perkin patentó su hallazgo en agosto de 1856 y, con el apoyo financiero de su padre, fundó una fábrica en 1857 para producir el colorante, inicialmente llamado púrpura de anilina y comercializado como mauve. El color violeta se volvió popular en Europa, especialmente entre las clases acomodadas, y la emperatriz Eugenia de Francia contribuyó a su difusión. item.description: Alejandro Elías Ponciano Pavo, taquígrafo español exiliado, falleció el 5 de mayo de 1945 en México, tras una larga enfermedad que lo había debilitado durante ocho meses. Su esposa, Carmen Jurado, y su hija, Magdalena, quedaron viudas e huérfanas, enfrentándose a una vida de miseria y dificultades. Carmen, refugiada política, tuvo que recurrir a otros exiliados republicanos para pagar los gastos del sepelio y la sepultura, ya que la comisión de ayuda de la CAFARE les concedió subsidios limitados y tardíos. La situación económica de Carmen se agravó tras la muerte de Alejandro, con crisis nerviosas y una dispepsia gástrica causada por su mala dentadura, a pesar de solicitar ayuda para tratamiento odontológico que le fue denegada. Las mujeres sobrevivían con trabajos de tejido a pedido y alquilando habitaciones a otros exiliados, compartiendo la misma habitación y comida cuando había. item.title: De los patios monásticos a los cementerios: la evolución de los claustros en la Edad Media
item.description: El artículo analiza cómo los claustros medievales en España, inicialmente espacios monásticos para la vida comunitaria, se transformaron en espacios funerarios a lo largo de los siglos. Según el texto, en el siglo XI, los nobles no podían enterrarse en el interior de las basílicas debido a la prohibición del Concilio de Braga de 561. Esto llevó a que los claustros, que originalmente eran patios cuadrangulares con galerías cubiertas anejos al templo, se convirtieran en lugares ideales para el descanso eterno. Los claustros servían para la circulación entre dependencias monásticas y, con el tiempo, se abrieron nichos funerarios (lucillos) en sus muros. A partir del siglo XII, los cabildos catedralicios comenzaron a secularizar los claustros, perdiendo la vida en comunidad y transformándose en espacios dedicados principalmente a sepulturas. En la catedral de Salamanca, se sistematizaron los nichos funerarios en el siglo XII, permitiendo a los compradores colocar sepulcros que podían ser m

item.title: Las pérdidas del Fondo E de las AFP chilenas superan el 10% en 2026 y ponen en alerta a cientos de miles de afiliados
item.description:
La crisis del Fondo E de las AFP chilenas golpea los ahorros de cientos de miles de afiliados y abre un debate sobre la gestión de las pensiones

La caída de los fondos de pensiones más conservadores de Chile ha encendido las alarmas entre jubilados y trabajadores próximos a retirarse. Las pérdidas acumuladas durante 2026, vinculadas a operaciones financieras sobre las tasas de interés de Estados Unidos, han afectado especialmente al Fondo E, considerado el de menor riesgo dentro del sistema de capitalización individual administrado por las Administradoras de Fondos de Pensiones (AFP).

Según cifras de la Superintendencia de Pensiones recogidas por medios chilenos, el Fondo E acumuló una rentabilidad real negativa del 10,39% entre enero y septiembre de 2026. La caída ha perjudicado a más de 760.000 afiliados que mantenían sus ahorros en esta cartera, entre ellos personas próximas a jubilarse y pensionistas que dependen de sus fondos para financiar sus ingresos

item.description:
La victoria demócrata en las elecciones de medio mandato de Estados Unidos abre un nuevo escenario político para Donald Trump. El vuelco electoral ha permitido al Partido Demócrata conquistar la mayoría en ambas cámaras del Congreso y arrebatar a los republicanos victorias en estados tradicionalmente conservadores. Sin embargo, el análisis sostiene que el principal derrotado no es necesariamente el Partido Republicano como organización, sino el trumpismo como proyecto político. La diferencia resulta fundamental para comprender el alcance de los resultados y los desafíos que se abren a partir de ahora.

item.title: Huelga general por el derecho a la vivienda y el empobrecimiento salarial
item.description: La huelga general convocada para el 11 de noviembre en España se presenta como una respuesta conjunta a la crisis habitacional y al empobrecimiento salarial que afecta a la clase trabajadora. El artículo analiza cómo el aumento de los precios de la vivienda y los productos básicos, junto con la depreciación de los salarios, han generado una situación crítica que afecta a millones de personas. Según datos del CIS, más del 55% de la población considera la vivienda como el problema más grave. El texto critica la especulación inmobiliaria, la turistificación de barrios y la falta de políticas públicas para garantizar el acceso a la vivienda. Además, señala que los salarios no han evolucionado al mismo ritmo que la inflación, con un ejemplo concreto en Correos donde los sueldos han caído un 25% desde 2008 en relación al IPC. La huelga busca romper la división entre trabajadores y promover una perspectiva social que reconozca que los problemas económicos son comunes a toda la clase trabajado

item.title: Carlos Cuerpo cesura al presidente de Adif tras asumir el ministerio de Transporte
item.description: El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha anunciado la designación del vicepresidente Carlos Cuerpo para asumir las competencias del ministerio de Transporte tras la dimisión de Óscar Puente. En su primera acción como titular del ministerio, Cuerpo ha decidido cesar al presidente de Adif, Luis Pedro Marco de la Peña, en una reunión con el secretario de Estado de Transportes, José Antonio Santano. Marco de la Peña, ingeniero de Caminos, Canales y Puertos, había sido viceconsejero de Infraestructuras y Transportes del Ejecutivo vasco antes de su nombramiento en Adif. Su carrera profesional incluye un periodo en Ferrovial, compañía especializada en infraestructuras, antes de incorporarse a otros sectores del sector de la construcción. La decisión de Cuerpo se produce en un contexto de reciente tragedia ferroviaria en Urda (Toledo), donde el accidente ha dejado víctimas y ha generado una gran preocupación pública. Cuerpo expresó en redes sociales su agradecimiento al presidente Sánchez

item.title: El diálogo filosófico como práctica activa en la construcción de la vida intelectual
item.description: La filosofía, según el texto, no debe entenderse como un conocimiento estático sino como un verbo activo que se conjuga en sus diversos tiempos. El autor, Diego Gracia, analiza la obra de Paolo Dordoni, 'Pratiche del confilosofare', destacando la importancia del diálogo socrático como método filosófico práctico. Gracia refiere a Xavier Zubiri, quien sostiene que la filosofía es algo que cada individuo debe construir personalmente, no un conocimiento que se puede aprender de forma pasiva. El texto subraya que no basta con estudiar filosofía en aulas o escribir sobre ella; es necesario vivir una experiencia filosófica activa que transforme la vida. Gracia compara la filosofía con el verbo, en contraste con los sustantivos estáticos, y cita a Kant y a Antonio Machado para reforzar esta idea. El autor también menciona la importancia de Sócrates como modelo de filosofía práctica, destacando que el diálogo filosófico genuino no es meramente un intercambio de ideas, sino una práctica que requ

item.title: Demócratas logran victoria histórica en Texas tras derrotar a Abbott y Paxton
item.description: Los demócratas han logrado una victoria histórica en Texas, uno de los principales bastiones republicanos de Estados Unidos, al conquistar la gobernación y una banca en el Senado después de más de tres décadas sin triunfos estatales. La legisladora estatal Gina Hinojosa, de 52 años y ascendencia mexicana, derrotó al gobernador Greg Abbott, figura influyente del Partido Republicano que ocupaba el cargo desde 2015. Por su parte, James Talarico, un seminarista presbiteriano de 37 años, se impuso al fiscal general Ken Paxton, estrecho aliado de Donald Trump respaldado económicamente por Elon Musk. Ambos se convirtieron en los primeros demócratas en ganar una elección estatal en Texas desde 1994. El partido también conquistó el cargo de fiscal general, avanzando en distritos legislativos y condados fronterizos con México. La victoria representa un duro revés para el presidente Donald Trump y abre un nuevo escenario político en un estado considerado durante años prácticamente inexpugnable pa

item.title: Murciélagos hibernan en la ciudadela de Spandau, Berlín, en un proyecto de voluntariado ambiental
item.description: La ciudadela de Spandau, una fortaleza renacentista ubicada al oeste de Berlín, alberga a miles de murciélagos que hibernan en sus sótanos durante el invierno. Jörg Harder, un agente de policía y voluntario, se encarga de cuidar a estos mamíferos voladores en un proyecto que busca desmitificar el miedo hacia ellos. Según Harder, los murciélagos son inofensivos y el lugar ofrece una exposición interactiva donde los visitantes pueden acariciarlos. La ciudadela, construida en el siglo XVI, es uno de los monumentos mejor preservados del Renacimiento europeo y cuenta con una historia militar ligada a la producción de armas desde 1722 hasta 1918. Spandau, una zona histórica con una identidad propia, se distingue por su orgullo local y su antigüedad, ya que existe desde 1197, antes que Berlín (1237). La zona, rodeada de edificios con cavidades y grietas ideales para la hibernación, alberga dieciocho de las veinticinco especies de murciélagos que habitan en Alemania. Harder explica que la cris

item.title: José Val del Omar: precursor del cine sensorial y creador de la técnica del zoom
item.description: José Val del Omar, un cineasta granadino nacido en 1904, es reconocido como un precursor del cine sensorial cuyas innovaciones técnicas anticiparon décadas el uso comercial de tecnologías que hoy son comunes en el cine. A los diez años, construyó una linterna mágica con materiales caseros, lo que marcó el inicio de su pasión por la proyección de imágenes. En 1928, a los 24 años, publicó en la revista La pantalla un artículo que destacaba sus innovaciones cinematográficas, incluyendo la creación del zoom óptico, técnica que permitía ampliar o recortar el encuadre sin mover físicamente la cámara. Esta invención, que se incorporó comercialmente décadas después, revolucionó la forma de filmar. Val del Omar también desarrolló la técnica de tactilvisión, que utilizaba luz pulsátil para crear sensación de relieve y profundidad en las imágenes, anticipando el cine 3D. Además, ideó el desbordamiento apanorámico, que proyectaba la película en la pantalla y en las paredes y techo de la sala, y el

item.title: Joven de ultraderecha agredido a Pablo Iglesias y detenido por robo de teléfono
item.description: Pablo Iglesias, político español, ha sido víctima de un intento de robo con violencia esta tarde en las inmediaciones de la estación de tren de Galapagar. Un joven de ideología ultraderecha comenzó a insultarle y a increparle mientras caminaba. Al momento de que Iglesias inició la grabación con su teléfono móvil, el joven intentó agredirle y sustrajo el dispositivo, huyendo a la carrera. Sin embargo, el político logró alcanzar al agresor junto con una persona que le acompañaba. La Guardia Civil acudió al lugar y trasladó al joven a dependencias del Instituto Armado en Galapagar. Iglesias ha anunciado que presentará una denuncia mañana contra el agresor. En declaraciones a Diario Red, el director del medio lamentó el auge del fascismo en algunos sectores de la juventud. Iglesias también compartió en su cuenta de Twitter que el joven le insultó mientras volvía a su casa, que intentó grabarle y que el agresor le quitó el teléfono huyendo, pero que finalmente fue detenido por la Guardia Ci

item.title: Daniel Monzón aborda en 'Ruega por nosotras' la historia silenciada del Patronato de Protección a la Mujer durante el franquismo
item.description: El cineasta Daniel Monzón, conocido por películas como 'Celda 211', presenta en el Festival de San Sebastián su nueva producción 'Ruega por nosotras', una película basada en hechos reales que explora la historia del Patronato de Protección a la Mujer durante el régimen franquista. La película, ambientada en 1974, sigue la historia de Ana, una joven de familia acomodada enviada a un reformatorio para mujeres 'caídas o en riesgo de caer', según la retórica nacionalcatólica. Monzón explica que la investigación para la película comenzó en 2020, con el estudio de tesis doctorales, libros de ensayo como los de Consuelo García del Cid, y testimonios de mujeres que pasaron por el Patronato. El director destaca que todo lo que se muestra en la película sucedió realmente, sin inventar nada. El Patronato, creado en 1940 por Carmen Polo de Franco, funcionó hasta 1985, incluso después de la muerte de Franco, lo que significa que niñas de la edad de Monzón eran encerradas y adoctrinadas mientras él

item.title: Elon Musk registra pérdida de más de 60.000 millones en patrimonio tras derrotas republicanas en elecciones de medio término
item.description: El magnate Elon Musk ha experimentado una significativa reducción en su patrimonio neto, superando los 60.000 millones de dólares, como consecuencia de los resultados electorales en las elecciones de medio término en Estados Unidos. Según el Financial Times, el empresario invirtió aproximadamente 446 millones de dólares en apoyar al Partido Republicano con el objetivo de mantener el control del Congreso, pero los resultados electorales, especialmente en Texas, donde los republicanos sufrieron una derrota significativa, han impactado negativamente en su fortuna. La caída en los mercados bursátiles de sus empresas principales ha agravado la situación: las acciones de Tesla cayeron un 5,7% y las de SpaceX disminuyeron un 7,6% en las primeras operaciones tras el resultado electoral. Además, el nuevo panorama político, con un Congreso controlado por los demócratas, podría generar mayor escrutinio legislativo sobre una posible fusión entre Tesla y SpaceX antes de 2029. Estos acontecimientos

item.title: La población mayor de 65 años en España supera el 20% y se prevé alcanzar el 30% en 20 años
item.description: El informe del Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (CSIC) sobre envejecimiento en España revela que la población de 65 años o más alcanzó 10.178.625 personas el 1 de enero de 2025, representando el 20,7% de la población total del país. Este dato marca un incremento de 250.257 personas respecto al año anterior, un 2,5% más. El informe, titulado 'Un perfil de las personas mayores en España, 2026', analiza demografía, salud, recursos económicos y condiciones de vida de la población mayor. La edad media de la población española llegó a 44,55 años en 2025, mientras que el número de centenarias aumentó un 7,1% en un año, pasando de 15.911 a 17.038, con el 80% siendo mujeres. Las proyecciones indican que para 2046, la población de 65 años o más superará los 16 millones, representando aproximadamente el 30% de la población total. En cuanto a vivienda, el 56,6% de los hogares con personas mayores se ubica en viviendas construidas antes de 1981, y solo el 20,7% ha realizado mejoras d

item.title: Feijóo critica gestión de Mazón y Gobierno central tras la dana de octubre
item.description: El presidente del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha expresado su crítica hacia la gestión del expresidente de la Generalitat, Carlos Mazón, y del Gobierno central en relación con la dana ocurrida en octubre de 2024, que provocó 234 muertes. En una entrevista en La Sexta, Feijóo aseguró que no ha avalado la gestión de Mazón y ha sido crítico tanto con la Generalitat Valenciana como con el Gobierno central. Destacó que, si volviera a llover con la misma intensidad que en la dana, se repetirían situaciones similares. Al ser preguntado sobre por qué Mazón no dimitió inmediatamente tras el desastre, Feijóo explicó que habían analizado la situación y tomado decisiones pertinentes. Señaló que el Gobierno de España no declaró la emergencia tras la dana, lo que, según él, contribuyó a la falta de respuesta adecuada. Además, Feijóo criticó que el ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, y el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, no asumen responsabilidades tras el accidente ferroviario d

item.title: Alcalde de Vigo advierte de que el suministro de agua de calidad se agotará en 22 días
item.description: El alcalde de Vigo, Abel Caballero, ha alertado de que la ciudad se encuentra en una situación 'extrema, límite' debido a la sequía, advirtiendo que solo quedan reservas suficientes para garantizar el suministro de agua de calidad óptima durante 22 días. El regidor ha criticado al presidente de la Xunta, Alfonso Rueda, por minimizar la gravedad de la sequía, calificando la situación de 'preocupación, pero no de emergencia', mientras que Caballero considera que el área de Vigo ya está en emergencia. El alcalde ha reclamado al Gobierno gallego que reduzca de inmediato el caudal ecológico, destacando que la potabilizadora construida por el Concello con una inversión de 25 millones de euros ha permitido mantener las garantías de calidad del suministro. Además, ha defendido las recomendaciones de consumo responsable implementadas desde julio, que han permitido ahorrar agua durante los últimos cuatro meses. Caballero ha acusado a la Xunta de 'gravísima negligencia' por no construir una nueva

item.title: Comisión Europea presenta guías para preparar a ciudadanos ante emergencias en tres días
item.description: La Comisión Europea ha presentado nuevas recomendaciones para que los ciudadanos puedan valerse por sí mismos durante las primeras 72 horas de una emergencia, con medidas que incluyen la preparación de kits de emergencia, la enseñanza en escuelas sobre cómo actuar ante catástrofes y la adaptación de sistemas de alerta y evacuación para personas con discapacidad. La comisaria europea de Preparación y Gestión de Crisis, Hadja Lahbib, presentó cuatro guías durante el noveno Foro Europeo de Protección Civil en Bruselas. Estas guías abordan la necesidad de que las familias tengan suministros básicos como agua, alimentos y medicamentos para tres días, así como planes familiares de emergencia y habilidades prácticas como primeros auxilios. Además, se propone integrar la preparación ante emergencias en el currículo escolar mediante actividades prácticas adaptadas a cada edad, sin crear una nueva asignatura. Otra guía se centra en adaptar los sistemas de alerta y evacuación para personas con di

item.title: Californianos rechazan propuesta de impuesto a la riqueza para financiar servicios públicos
item.description: Los ciudadanos de California han votado en contra de la Proposición 40, que proponía establecer un impuesto del 5% sobre los patrimonios superiores a 1.000 millones de dólares, con el objetivo de financiar programas sociales como Medi-Cal, asistencia alimentaria y educación. La iniciativa, que habría afectado a aproximadamente 200 personas, principalmente empresarios tecnológicos de Silicon Valley, prometía recaudar 100.000 millones de dólares en cinco años. Los opositores, liderados por figuras como Sergey Brin (fundador de Google), Peter Thiel (Palantir) y Eric Schmidt (ex CEO de Google), reunieron 333 millones de dólares para su campaña, frente a los 33 millones de los promotores de la propuesta. Además, los opositores impulsaron otras iniciativas como la Proposición 41, que limita el gasto público, y la Proposición 42, que prohíbe nuevos impuestos sobre la propiedad personal y los impuestos retroactivos. La Proposición 42 fue la única aprobada, reflejando una clara preferencia por

item.title: Kast, Abascal y la Fundación Disenso: los vínculos políticos detrás de la Carta de Madrid
item.description:
La relación entre José Antonio Kast y Santiago Abascal vuelve a poner en el foco a la Fundación Disenso y a la denominada Carta de Madrid, una iniciativa impulsada por Vox para articular una alianza política entre dirigentes de Hispanoamérica y España. El encuentro entre ambos líderes, celebrado antes de que Kast acudiera a recibir una medalla de Isabel Díaz Ayuso, sirve como punto de partida para examinar los vínculos entre sus proyectos políticos y el papel de esta fundación.

La Fundación Disenso y la Carta de Madrid

Santiago Abascal, líder de Vox, creó en 2020 la Fundación Disenso, una organización que ocupa un lugar relevante en la estrategia política e ideológica del partido. Desde esta entidad se promovió la Carta de Madrid, un manifiesto que describe la denominada iberosfera como un espacio supuestamente amenazado por regímenes totalitarios de inspiración comunista.

El documento plantea una visión política compartida entre España

item.title: Ataque cibernético a bancos de sangre franceses frustrado antes de causar daños, según autoridades
item.description: La noticia relata un incidente en el que un ataque cibernético a los sistemas de refrigeración de bancos de sangre en Francia fue frustrado antes de causar daños significativos. Según las autoridades, los sistemas de refrigeración, suministrados por una empresa externa, fueron objeto de un ataque que podría haber afectado a los suministros de plasma médico. Los comentarios de WendyErikaM, que aparecen en la noticia, destacan que los atacantes no necesitaron penetrar los sistemas propios del servicio de sangre, sino que explotaron vulnerabilidades en el equipo de refrigeración proporcionado por una compañía externa. Esto plantea preocupaciones sobre la seguridad de infraestructuras médicas críticas que dependen de equipos remotos accesibles. Los sistemas de alarma independientes y la intervención rápida evitaron que los productos sanguíneos vitales se dañaran. WendyErikaM señala que este incidente representa una escalada preocupante en el cibercrimen, ya que no se trata de datos robados

item.title: Centro de reclutamiento militar en Kiev: vídeo viral confunde manifestante con víctima de tortura
item.description: La noticia aborda la difusión de un vídeo en redes sociales que supuestamente mostraba la liberación de 40 militares ucranianos torturados en un centro en Petropavlivska Borshchahivka, cerca de Kiev. La policía ucraniana y periodistas independientes han desmentido estas afirmaciones. Según el periodista Francis Farrell del Kyiv Independent, el joven que aparece en el vídeo envuelto en una manta, presentado como víctima, era en realidad un manifestante que lanzaba ladrillos contra el edificio durante una protesta. El adolescente, de 14 años, confirmó en vídeos publicados en TikTok que acudió voluntariamente a la protesta, trepó la valla y fue golpeado por personas desconocidas, no por militares. La policía explicó que el inmueble funcionaba como alojamiento temporal para militares de la Guardia Nacional antes de su traslado a formación básica, negando detenciones ilegales o torturas. item.title: Centros de datos en auge: riesgo de duplicar el consumo eléctrico doméstico en España
item.description: La noticia aborda la preocupación creciente sobre el impacto del aumento en la cantidad de centros de datos en el consumo eléctrico en España. Según el texto, la proliferación de estos centros, especialmente los de gran tamaño o 'hiperescala', está generando un aumento significativo en el consumo energético, lo que podría traducirse en un incremento de hasta el doble en las facturas eléctricas para los usuarios finales. Aunque el artículo menciona que inicialmente se centró en el consumo de agua por parte de estos centros en países como Países Bajos, Chile y Uruguay, el foco principal de la noticia se centra en el impacto eléctrico en España. El texto señala que las comunidades agrícolas en esos países se vieron afectadas por el consumo de agua, pero no profundiza en cómo esto se relaciona con el consumo eléctrico en España. La noticia parece estar incompleta, ya que termina abruptamente con una invitación a suscribirse para seguir leyendo, lo que sugiere que el contenido proporcionado

item.title: Deb Haaland se convierte en la primera gobernadora indígena de Nuevo México tras victoria en elecciones
item.description: Las elecciones de medio término en Estados Unidos han marcado hitos históricos en la representación política. Deb Haaland, demócrata y miembro de la comunidad indígena, ha ganado las elecciones para gobernadora de Nuevo México, convirtiéndose en la primera mujer indígena en alcanzar este cargo. Antes de su elección, Haaland ocupó la Secretaría de Interior en la administración del expresidente Joe Biden, siendo la primera nativa americana en formar parte del Gabinete estadounidense. Durante su mandato en el Departamento de Interior, impulsó investigaciones sobre los internados forzosos que separaron a niños indígenas de sus comunidades, produciendo dos informes oficiales y el proyecto 'Road to Healing'. También amplió los acuerdos de cogestión de tierras con pueblos originarios, pasando de 20 a 300, y promovió la Unidad de Personas Desaparecidas y Asesinadas para investigar casos de violencia contra mujeres indígenas. item.title: Bassem Youssef utiliza la ironía para cuestionar las aspiraciones territoriales de Daniela Weiss
item.description:
La intervención de Bassem Youssef en el programa de Piers Morgan se convirtió en un ejercicio de sátira política en el que el humorista egipcio utilizó la ironía para cuestionar las posiciones de Daniela Weiss, una de las figuras del movimiento de colonización israelí. El intercambio giró en torno a la expansión territorial, la soberanía sobre Gaza y Cisjordania y las declaraciones de Weiss sobre el futuro de los palestinos.

El encuentro, comentado posteriormente por los presentadores de un vídeo de análisis, puso de manifiesto el contraste entre las afirmaciones explícitas de Weiss y la estrategia de Youssef, que optó por aparentar admiración hacia sus planteamientos para subrayar sus implicaciones políticas y humanitarias.

Daniela Weiss y la expansión de los asentamientos

La conversación comienza con Daniela Weiss conectada desde un puesto avanzado en Gaza, al que identifica como Gaza Pioneers. Desde allí describe su intención de avanzar hacia el norte

item.title: El legado filosófico de 'Hacedor de Estrellas' en la ciencia ficción clásica
item.description: La noticia analiza la obra 'Hacedor de Estrellas' (1937) del escritor Olaf Stapledon, considerada una de las obras maestras de la ciencia ficción clásica. El texto explora cómo Stapledon, un profesor de Filosofía de la Universidad de Liverpool, abordó conceptos que la astronomía tardaría décadas en confirmar, como la existencia de múltiples universos y la inhumanidad del cosmos. La novela, que no sigue una trama convencional sino que presenta una visión filosófica del universo, describe un viaje mental a través del tiempo y el espacio, desde el Big Bang hasta el vacío final, donde el narrador descubre que el 'Hacedor de Estrellas' crea y descarta universos sin piedad hacia las formas de vida que en ellos habitan. Stapledon, influenciado por pensadores como Giordano Bruno, plantea una visión radical del lugar del ser humano en el cosmos, destacando su insignificancia ante la inmensidad del universo. La obra, poco conocida por el público general pero reverenciada por críticos y académico

item.title: Universidades públicas madrileñas se suman a huelga general por falta de financiación
item.description: Las seis universidades públicas madrileñas (UAH, UAM, UCM, UC3M, UPM y URJC) han anunciado su participación en la huelga educativa general en la Comunidad de Madrid, que comenzará este miércoles y se extenderá hasta el jueves. Los docentes y estudiantes se movilizarán para denunciar la «asfixia económica» que sufren las instituciones universitarias públicas debido a la infrafinanciación por parte del Gobierno regional. Las protestas incluyen piquetes informativos en las universidades, una marcha desde la sede del PSOE hasta la del PP, y una concentración frente a la Consejería de Educación. Las plataformas en defensa de la educación pública critican el acuerdo de financiación plurianual firmado el 3 de marzo entre el Gobierno regional y los rectores, que consideran insuficiente al mantenerse en el 0,4% del PIB, muy por debajo del 1% establecido en la LOSU y de la media nacional y europea.
